resolution:
NOT a preexisting main break, and NOT caused by your diff. Do NOT wait for a hotfix and do NOT change any code. Your work is complete and correct — just re-run verify.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED. The verify run did not finish. It ABORTED at 47% — only 6975 of 14703 collected tests ran — because a pytest-xdist worker died. attempt-1.orchestrator.test.log carries "[gw14] node down: Not properly terminated" and "worker 'gw14' crashed while running tests/test_merge_queue_restart_hook.py::test_stop_does_not_preempt_finalizing_head_mid_advance". Host load average was 96/128/152 (and 133 while I was measuring) on a 32-core box — 3-5x oversubscribed. All 12 reported failures are timing-sensitive async merge-queue / liveness / offline-lane tests starving under that contention.

MEASUREMENTS I TOOK IN YOUR WORKTREE (branch task/3514, all green):
- The 12 named failing tests, re-run in isolation: 20 passed in 15.15s.
- All 96 tests in the 7 affected files, run in full: 96 passed in 24.51s.
- Your own touched files (test_conftest_helpers, test_out_of_band_routing, test_steward, test_suggestion_triage, test_workflow_state_machine_boundary): 308 passed.
- lint rc=0 and type rc=0 already, per attempt-1.orchestrator.summary.json.

WHY IT IS NOT YOUR DIFF. git diff main...HEAD touches exactly four test files: orchestrator/tests/conftest.py, test_conftest_helpers.py, test_out_of_band_routing.py, test_steward.py. None of the seven failing files is among them, and none of them references make_steward or TaskSteward. Your conftest.py change is entirely inside the make_steward fixture body plus an inert module-level `import json` and a `stamp_stock_routing_config` import — no autouse fixture, no session-scoped or global state, so it cannot reach an unrelated merge-queue test.

WHY IT WAS MISLABELLED "preexisting on main". verify_failure_is_preexisting_on_main re-ran the failure on a _mainprobe- worktree of main and compared (category, normalised cause_hint). Under this load the same timing tests starved on main too, the signatures matched, and it returned (True, main_sha) -> await_preexisting_main_hotfix. Main is not red; the probe just reproduced the same load flake on both sides. Separately, the task-2365 xdist-crash auto-retry did not fire because _is_bare_xdist_worker_crash vetoes once any FAILED line names a test outside the single-entry _KNOWN_LOAD_FLAKE_NODEID_RES allow-list, and twelve unlisted flakes co-occurred with the crash. This is a well-precedented class here (done tasks 2365, 2376, 2350, 2921, 2959, 2320). I filed ticket tkt_0RS1ADE3BF2PW9W6FN1H9215KZ to apply task 2370's isolated-re-run confirm gate to that probe so this stops wedging tasks.

WHAT TO DO NOW: re-run verify unchanged (`cd orchestrator && uv run pytest tests/ -q` plus `uv run ruff check tests/`). The re-run is genuinely necessary, not a formality — more than half the suite never executed against your branch, so it still needs a clean full pass. If a worker crashes again under load, that is the same infra flake, not a regression: re-run rather than sending it to the debugger, and escalate again only if a failure reproduces on an ISOLATED (-n0) re-run.
